# kopia_notification_test (Action)

Has the Kopia server send its test notification through a stored notification profile, to prove that the profile delivers: after it is created, after a change to the mail server or the network, or on demand.

This is a Terraform *action*, not a resource, and needs **Terraform 1.14 or newer**. It runs only when invoked — from a resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` or with `terraform apply -invoke=action.kopia_notification_test.<name>` — and remembers nothing afterwards. It reads the profile from Kopia and posts it to `POST /api/v1/testNotificationProfile`, the call behind the test button of the Kopia UI: Kopia builds a sender from the profile and delivers its test message through it, whatever the profile's `min_severity`, and the invocation fails when it cannot. Any email, Pushover or webhook profile can be tested, whether `kopia_notification_profile` manages it or it was set up in the Kopia UI or with the CLI.

~> **Every invocation delivers a real message.** Trigger it on `after_create` and `after_update` of the profile, or invoke it by hand, rather than on every apply.

Kopia waits for the delivery without an overall time limit of its own — for email, without any — so the provider's `request_timeout` bounds the test; when it expires, the outcome is unknown and the message may still arrive. Kopia quotes a profile's settings in some of its errors, so the secrets among them — SMTP password, Pushover tokens, webhook URL and headers — are replaced with `<redacted>` in the errors the action reports.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Actions need Terraform 1.14 or newer. The action keeps no state, and every
# invocation delivers a real test message.
resource "kopia_notification_profile" "ops" {
  name         = "ops"
  min_severity = "warning"

  webhook = {
    endpoint = "https://ntfy.example.org/kopia-backups"
    headers = {
      Authorization = "Bearer ${var.ntfy_token}"
    }
  }

  # Test the profile once it is saved, and again after every change. The action
  # reads the profile's name, so it has to run after the profile is saved;
  # before_create would be a cycle.
  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.kopia_notification_test.ops]
    }
  }
}

action "kopia_notification_test" "ops" {
  config {
    name = kopia_notification_profile.ops.name
  }
}

# Any email, Pushover or webhook profile can be tested, including one set up in
# the Kopia UI, on demand with:
#
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.kopia_notification_test.mail
action "kopia_notification_test" "mail" {
  config {
    name = "mail"
  }
}

variable "ntfy_token" {
  description = "Access token of the ntfy topic."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the notification profile to test, as `kopia_notification_profile` and the `kopia_notification_profiles` data source show it; case-sensitive. The profile must exist when the action runs: to test one created in the same apply, trigger the action from that `kopia_notification_profile` on `after_create`, with its `name` here.
